Alldays Orphanage

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Millions donated for an orphanage that doesn't exist!

Unique Selling Point:
Swedish national Lief Rahmqvist is one of the biggest private landowners in the Limpopo Province. In 1994 he bought up a bunch of farms on the Botswana border, North of Alldays, in the Blouberg Local Municipality. He consolidated them into what he called the Mapungubwe Private Nature Reserve (PTY) Ltd. The property borders the Mapungubwe National Park. In 2013 decided to "give back" to the community of Alldays. He founded the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre NPO. In essence, he took over the established Dirisang Drop-in centre that has been around for years... And he proceeded to get donations from far and wide

Summary:
The Dirisang Drop-in Centre is a registered NPO with the Limpopo DSD, and for years, two volunteers, Stephen Serakalala and Paulina Manengene have been feeding kids from a little shack next to the Alldays Primary School. They also offer homework support to some of the most vulnerable children in Alldays... Come rain or shine, meals are cooked in the open and kids sit there on the dusty ground enjoying what is often their only meal for the day.

In 2013 Rahmqvist swooped in as the saviour of these children. He founded the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre (NPO) and Stephen and Paulina were given positions on the board. (along with other municipal officers). And the building was built on Municipal land right next to the Alldays Primary School.

Further information:
Today, Paulina and Stephen are still feeding 109 of the most vulnerable children in Alldays. Except, they do it in the dust NEXT TO the building built for them. They are not allowed to use the facility at all. They erected a tin shack from where they cook on gas (no electricity). They get water from a neighbour in a blue drum that they roll down the street once a week, as they are not allowed to access the water on the property. The children are also not allowed to use the ablution facilities (built for them)... so once again, Stephen managed to get 2x bucket toilets donated... and this is what the kids have to use.

So, how is it possible that a haven was built for these kids in Alldays, but they have no access to it... in the meantime Rahmqvist boasts about his "Orphanage in South Africa" on social media. Even his lawyer, Hennie Erwee, names the "Orphanage" as his CSI project.

Rahmqvist now lives abroad, but visits his farm regularly. When he has guests, he likes to take them to his Orphanage. The Orphanage Mother, Sarkie, then arranges children to come hang out at the building during the day for the publicity... in the evening, when the guests have left, they go home. These kids are not orphans. And the facility is not registered with DSD.

What is registered is the Dirisang Drop-In Centre which operates in the corner of the property, while Sarkie pretty much lives alone in the building.

When Rahmqvist set out to build the "Orphanage" he engaged with the municipality and got permission to use the land. He got a Swedish architect and local contractors to build his orphanage... All along, he maintained that he wanted to retain sole power, but this is not how NPO's work. The Mapungubwe Foundation NPO Board consists of Rahmqvist, his lawyer, Hennie Erwee, Stephen and Paulina from the Dirisang Drop-In Centre, 2 gentlemen from the Blouberg Local Municipality and 2 others. Mr Machaba -- who was the Blouberg Municipal Manager at the time -- was elected as Chairman of the Board... and he still is...

In 2013 Rahmqvist started building his Orphanage. The original plan was to build an orphanage for 300 kids... But eventually a building was built with room for about 10 girls and 10 boys. At the same time, he decided to build a lodge (Lesedi Lodge) on one of his farms. He made a deal with all contractors working on the Orphanage that he would deduct a donation of 6.5% from their fee as a donation to the orphanage. Emails also show other donations from various international individuals and companies.

In 2014 a container with donated goods, including 40 beds arrived from Sweden. Even though Rahmqvist sent a letter to the Department of Trade and Industry, declaring that the beds were a donation to be used in the Orphanage... and even though he advertised on social media about the generous donation of beds... The beds were taken to Lesedi Lodge.


In 2008 Micawber 639 (PTY) Ltd applied for prospecting rights on Rahmqvist's property, which was granted. One of the directors of Micawber 639 is Hendrik Marthinus Erwee (Hennie Erwee) who also happens to be Rahmqvist's lawyer. In 2013 when Rahmqvist started with the "orphanage", a young Indian mining company wanted to prospect for coal on Rahmqvist's land. IG Resources FZE negotiated with Rahmqvist and Erwee and they were given permission to prospect under the mining licence of Micawber 639. They also generously committed to paying a R2.9 million donation to Rahmqvist's "Orphanage"...

Websites, and press releases and newspaper articles painted Rahmqvist a saint, a saviour.

Rahmqvist also insisted that all his staff and even the hunters hired to facilitate hunts on his farms, pay a 6.5% donation to the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre / Orphanage.

Rahmqvist boasts online about his CSI project, helping desperate children. The international company (which was started by Erik Rahmqvist) lists the "Orphanage" as their main CSI project. Mr Erwee (attorney and Mining Director) also owns a company called The Ark Wildlife Exporters, facilitating hunts, and the export of hunting trophies... And yes... he also brags about the Alldays Orphanage on his company/s websites.

Everyone, it seems, is using these hungry, desperate children to score brownie points with the outside world!

But the not-so-funny thing is... It's been a decade and those kids are still fed from a little shack on the side of the property. In 40degrees they sit in the sun, Meters away from the building, doing their homework, eating the meal that Paulina and Stephen prepared in a make-shift kitchen.

Rahmqvist was not transparent about the donations received and fights broke out between him and the other board members. And even though the other Board Members instituted a Vote of No Confidence in Rahmqvist and Erwee, the 2 are still in charge.

The Hawks have been investigating. Nature conservation is investigating various transgressions, from illegal logging on his farm, to illegal logging inside Botswana, to illegal Hunts on his farm...

And while everyone drag their feet, the building stands almost empty and Rahmqvist and Erwee have time to cover their tracks.

The 25000HA farm is listed as for sale -- for US$58 million
Rahmqvist has instigated litigation against those who speak out.

Erwee is good friends with Dawie Groenewald -- SA Rhino Poacher No.1 & John Hume, Mr Rhino Breeder... Erwee's company - The Ark Wildlife Exporters has an office in China.

Rahmqvist's farm borders the Mapungubwe National Park and Mapungubwe has rhinos and few fences...

In the meantime Rahmqvist has handed over the management of the "Orphanage" to NorSA, an NGO run by Erwee's ex-wife, Marietjie Bezuidenhout... Without the consent of the other board members.

Script:


s
ALLDAYS “ORPHANAGE” – Script FINAL


PROMO VIDEO
I’ve been in Africa for 25 years…
One day I visited the high school and met the headmaster and he said they going to close drop-in centr and 160 children is there and they’re going to be thrown out, almost dying on the street, you know, no-one is going to take care of them.. Then I said let me try to do something for those kids…
MUSIC


V/O
This is Paulina Manengena’s life…
Paulina
I have been working here for 15 years..


Every week – Monday to Friday – she comes here, to her corrugated iron kitchen to cook for the children of Alldays …
Paulina
We have 114 kids that we are taking care of.
V/O
Paulina manages the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre – a registered NPO with the Limpopo Provincial Department of Social Development.
It is essentially a community-driven aftercare service in Alldays, in Northern Limpopo…. giving vulnerable children a safe place to go after school, offering homework assistance and food…
For many this is the only meal of the day…
Paulina
One person brings a cabbage, another one brings green pepp er, another person brings carrots, and we are able to cook. We just have to persevere and sacrifice.
V/O
About a decade ago ... Paulina & the children’s lives were supposed to change drastically, when THIS wealthy Swedish businessman - Leif Rahmqvist - arrived with promises…
Paulina
He explained that he has interest in working with us, and he has already asked for donations from abroad. He wants to use those donations to help us.

We told him that our biggest wish is to have a building, because we are working in a shack.

Masa 06:09 to 06:18

At that time Ms Paulina how did you feel when this man promised to construct a building, and you have this land, and the municipality is also involved.

Paulina 06:19 to 06:45

I was very happy. I told myself that I would be stress-free, and that everything would finally be in place.
V/O
Rahmqvist negotiated with the local municipality to construct a building… for the Drop-In Centre… on Municipal land.
LINK
This so-called orphanage was built for these kids over here. Except many of them aren’t actually orphans and they haven’t even seen the inside of the building…
V/O
A decade after this building was constructed, the kids are still outside in the hot Limpopo sun.

Stephen Serakalala is the community elected chair of the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre…
Stephen
Masa: What’s in this building?

It's a nice, uh, kitchen with nice kitchen unit, everything is nice inside… everything is nice, right for the kids…
V/O
The original Management plan, approved by the Blouberg Local Municipality, estimated that around R15 million would be spent, and the facility would include a clinic, education and training facilities …and a soccer field.
LINK
Who is Leif Rahmqvist… Well, he’s a Swedish businessman who purchased a string of farms in Northern Limpopo in 1995. And while here he documented his time in Africa in this book – Mapungubwe – Place of the stone of wisdom –... Here’s a little extract:
“Sixty years ago in his native Stockholm a young Leif Rahmqvist visited his suburban local theatre where he watched his first Tarzan movie. This movie inspired him to one day visit the “Dark Continent”.
V/O
From the start, Rahmqvist was actively raising funds for this project. His Europe-based company, Rahmqvist International listed the “Orphanage” as one of its flagship CSI projects. Social media posts with Nordic bank accounts were asking for donations…
Eugene
At that stage Mr Rahmqvist already told everybody that he’s got a lot of money, from donors, that were ready for this project.
V/O
Eugene Small is a professional hunter, and was working for Rahmqvist, overseeing the construction of the so-called “orphanage” in Alldays.
Eugene
You know, Mr Rahmqvist is a good businessman, very good, you know. So his whole idea was everybody must help. The people in the community, contractors and stuff that was here, everybody had to pay 6.5% of the invoices… even the professional hunters that worked here, you know, they were deducted 6.5% from their payment…
LINK
No one is exactly sure how much was donated, or where all the monies ended up, but emails between Rahmqvist and donors point to sizeable amounts that flowed in from abroad – all of it to supposedly help THESE children...
V/O
At the end of 2014 a container filled with donated goods from Sweden arrived at Durban Harbour…
Stephen
We were having a meeting at the municipality with his lawyer. He said there is a luggage for the kids that needs us to form a board and constitution at the same time…
V/O
A non profit company needed to be registered to clear the donations with customs.

Eight board members were appointed to manage this NPC – called “The Mapungubwe Foundation”

Leif Rahmqvist, his Lawyer, Hennie Erwee, two members of the Blouberg Local Municipality, 2 local community members representing Social Services … and Stephen and Paulina..
Paulina
We quickly signed that constitution. As a board member I can’t even tell you what was in those parcels. I don’t know anything.

Masa: So you did not understand some of the things that you were told to do or sign because everything was rushed.

Paulina 21:46 to 22:04

Yes, everything he did, he hijacked it. When you are sitting down doing something else they will come and suggest drafting something quickly.

We were excited, thinking that everything would run smoothly, but those rushed decisions brought us problems.
V/O
The Dirisanang Drop-In Centre was now tied to Rahmqvist, and he wanted to be in control…

Legal Services Manager at the Blouberg Local Municipality, Mike Makwela, is also a board member of the Mapungubwe Foundation.
Mike Makwela
We were just stooges because we didn’t take any decisions in a conglomerated fashion… Decisions were taking by Rahmqvist together maybe with Erwee, but I think I should believe it’s Leif in particular…
V/O
Rahmqvist even demanded Veto rights as a member of the Mapungubwe Foundation board…
Eugene
I think Mr. Rahmqvist wasn't going to let anybody share his idea, share his running of this place, So there were quite a lot of conflict from the early meetings…
Makwela
I remember in one previous meeting wherein Leif just banged the door and went out because we said we wanted to see financial statement. And then he said no, I'll also want to see financial statement of Dirisanang.”.

Are you telling me that this man displayed such arrogance towards this community and the local municipality did nothing but watched.

00:17:56:06 - 00:18:35:06
Speaker 2
And know the local news to actually do to foot with your first question? Yes, he displays arrogance, but the municipality did almost everything in its power to make it a point that it brings them to the table…





V/O
By 2015 the relationship between The Drop-In Centre and Rahmqvist was crumbling.

Rahmqvist appointed Sarkie Mateke as Orphanage mother… which meant that 2 different charities were operating from the same municipal property – Rahmqvist’s Orphanage inside the newly constructed building … and the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre, in a corrugated iron shack along the fence of the property.
V/O
Manager of the Blouberg Municipality satellite office in Alldays, Frans Mphateng stepped in during our interview with Makwela to help explain the situation….
Frans Mphateng

Frans: The thing is, some of the things were like hearsay up until we realised but this thing is real. Because we went there and Manangena took us along throughout that building and we could see that really, they are not utilising that very big building…
V/O
Despite the issues, Rahmqvist has over the years, brought many international guests to visit “his orphanage”...
Paulina
Every year, we will have visitors from Sweden coming in to check if work is being done, and they donate money.

As we speak, they were here on Friday. A lot of white people were here on Friday. On Saturday they left and went to the farm.


V/O
While we were filming in Alldays, Rahmqvist was treating his guests to his extravagant 80th Birthday celebrations…
BIRTHDAY CLIP


V/O
The community alleges that, when guests visit, children are enticed to spend an hour or two at the orphanage, to sing and pose for pictures… all to impress would-be donors…
Stephen
This guy, he gets lot of millions using our kids, and at the end our kids get nothing…
V/O
Rahmqvist responded in writing via his lawyer, Hennie Erwee. He denies all allegations and says the Drop-In Centre children are welcome at his facility.

Both Erwee and Rahmqvist emphatically deny benefiting financially from any donations received for the orphanage, all of which can be accounted for… and they offered this video from the birthday celebrations, presumably as proof that Rahmqvist is supporting the community…
UPS VIDEO
“Happy Birthday, Father, and I thank God for giving us a father like you. And we thank you for the home you give us.”
V/O
Behind the girl giving the birthday wishes is Orphanage Mother, Sarkie Mateke. She claims she’s currently taking care of 19 children in the so-called Orphanage…
V/O
According to Rahmqvist and Erwee, all allegations against them are part of a smear campaign by former employee Eugene Small… Rahmqvist says he is suing Small for R30 million, which Small owes him…

But Eugene maintains it’s a matter of principle…


Eugene
The main thing is people go out there, they gloat about what they’re doing. They write articles in magazines about what they do and how great they are. And the children who are supposed to benefit from the beginning, from 2014 that they're supposed to benefit, eat on the ground.


V/O
Rahmqvist and Erwee add that no children are deliberately sourced to mislead donors, and all donations received have been spent on running the orphanage, and other initiatives via a different NPC, The Rahmqvist Foundation.

They claim the community members of the Mapungubwe Foundation board were eager to gain control of funds and ignored their attempts to convene board meetings.


Frans Mphateng
Masa: What are you going to do to make sure that those children, this winter, are not inside that shack…

Frans: Like MAkwela has just said, the matter is with the HAWKS, what was left now was for the council to take a decision on whether to tell him to move out in terms of the document.

Masa: Isn’t it a no-brainer that he should move out?

Frans: No, in a case… as you are dealing with a case you can’t just abruptly say no today you must go…

Masa: It’s not abrupt. I’m saying this thing has been going on since 2015, 2014. That’s a long time ago, Sir.

Frans: Those were not… they were issues that we were discussing, we were trying to resolve…

Masa: Had it been nipped in the bud then, do you think we’d be sitting in this position where you now have to get a council meeting to get rid of this man…

Farns: Unless you realise that something really fishy is happening..

Masa: It’s really fishy… we spent 2 days..




Frans: It’s really fishy because we can all agree. That’s why we are saying we took the matter to the HAWKS.
V/O
The Hawks have confirmed that they are investigating the case, but could not give us any further information…

And while board members are fighting and sending letters, pointing fingers at each other, the children of the Dirisinang Drop-In Centre are grateful for the little that they have… And Paulina and Stephen continue to fight for them…
Stephen



My wish is to die, this problem being solved.. If I can die, this problem not being solved… I think I can be a ghost…






PROMOS
PROMO 1 11”
A so-called “Orphanage”, equipped with facilities, built specifically to improve the lives of these children…

UPSOUND : STEPHEN
Everything is nice inside… right for the kids

So why are they not using it?
PROMO 2 21”
A registered NPO feeding over 100 vulnerable children, a multimillion rand centre built for them and the municipality that provided the land

UPSOUND STEPHEN
We were excited, very excited.. Everyone in the community we were very happy…

So why are these children unable to access the building that was intended for them?





PROMO 3 21”
With no running water and no electricity a group of volunteers are feeding over 100 kids in the Alldays Community…
UPSOUND: PAULINA

This, right next to a R6 million building, constructed to benefit these children!

2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: s ALLDAYS “ORPHANAGE” – Script FINAL PROMO VIDEO I’ve been in Africa for 25 years… One day I visited the high school and met the headmaster and he said they going to close drop-in centr and 160 children is there and they’re going to be thrown out, almost dying on the street, you know, no-one is going to take care of them.. Then I said let me try to do something for those kids… MUSIC V/O This is Paulina Manengena’s life… Paulina I have been working here for 15 years.. Every week – Monday to Friday – she comes here, to her corrugated iron kitchen to cook for the children of Alldays … Paulina We have 114 kids that we are taking care of. V/O Paulina manages the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre – a registered NPO with the Limpopo Provincial Department of Social Development. It is essentially a community-driven aftercare service in Alldays, in Northern Limpopo…. giving vulnerable children a safe place to go after school, offering homework assistance and food… For many this is the only meal of the day… Paulina One person brings a cabbage, another one brings green pepp er, another person brings carrots, and we are able to cook. We just have to persevere and sacrifice. V/O About a decade ago ... Paulina & the children’s lives were supposed to change drastically, when THIS wealthy Swedish businessman - Leif Rahmqvist - arrived with promises… Paulina He explained that he has interest in working with us, and he has already asked for donations from abroad. He wants to use those donations to help us. We told him that our biggest wish is to have a building, because we are working in a shack. Masa 06:09 to 06:18 At that time Ms Paulina how did you feel when this man promised to construct a building, and you have this land, and the municipality is also involved. Paulina 06:19 to 06:45 I was very happy. I told myself that I would be stress-free, and that everything would finally be in place. V/O Rahmqvist negotiated with the local municipality to construct a building… for the Drop-In Centre… on Municipal land. LINK This so-called orphanage was built for these kids over here. Except many of them aren’t actually orphans and they haven’t even seen the inside of the building… V/O A decade after this building was constructed, the kids are still outside in the hot Limpopo sun. Stephen Serakalala is the community elected chair of the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre… Stephen Masa: What’s in this building? It's a nice, uh, kitchen with nice kitchen unit, everything is nice inside… everything is nice, right for the kids… V/O The original Management plan, approved by the Blouberg Local Municipality, estimated that around R15 million would be spent, and the facility would include a clinic, education and training facilities …and a soccer field. LINK Who is Leif Rahmqvist… Well, he’s a Swedish businessman who purchased a string of farms in Northern Limpopo in 1995. And while here he documented his time in Africa in this book – Mapungubwe – Place of the stone of wisdom –... Here’s a little extract: “Sixty years ago in his native Stockholm a young Leif Rahmqvist visited his suburban local theatre where he watched his first Tarzan movie. This movie inspired him to one day visit the “Dark Continent”. V/O From the start, Rahmqvist was actively raising funds for this project. His Europe-based company, Rahmqvist International listed the “Orphanage” as one of its flagship CSI projects. Social media posts with Nordic bank accounts were asking for donations… Eugene At that stage Mr Rahmqvist already told everybody that he’s got a lot of money, from donors, that were ready for this project. V/O Eugene Small is a professional hunter, and was working for Rahmqvist, overseeing the construction of the so-called “orphanage” in Alldays. Eugene You know, Mr Rahmqvist is a good businessman, very good, you know. So his whole idea was everybody must help. The people in the community, contractors and stuff that was here, everybody had to pay 6.5% of the invoices… even the professional hunters that worked here, you know, they were deducted 6.5% from their payment… LINK No one is exactly sure how much was donated, or where all the monies ended up, but emails between Rahmqvist and donors point to sizeable amounts that flowed in from abroad – all of it to supposedly help THESE children... V/O At the end of 2014 a container filled with donated goods from Sweden arrived at Durban Harbour… Stephen We were having a meeting at the municipality with his lawyer. He said there is a luggage for the kids that needs us to form a board and constitution at the same time… V/O A non profit company needed to be registered to clear the donations with customs. Eight board members were appointed to manage this NPC – called “The Mapungubwe Foundation” Leif Rahmqvist, his Lawyer, Hennie Erwee, two members of the Blouberg Local Municipality, 2 local community members representing Social Services … and Stephen and Paulina.. Paulina We quickly signed that constitution. As a board member I can’t even tell you what was in those parcels. I don’t know anything. Masa: So you did not understand some of the things that you were told to do or sign because everything was rushed. Paulina 21:46 to 22:04 Yes, everything he did, he hijacked it. When you are sitting down doing something else they will come and suggest drafting something quickly. We were excited, thinking that everything would run smoothly, but those rushed decisions brought us problems. V/O The Dirisanang Drop-In Centre was now tied to Rahmqvist, and he wanted to be in control… Legal Services Manager at the Blouberg Local Municipality, Mike Makwela, is also a board member of the Mapungubwe Foundation. Mike Makwela We were just stooges because we didn’t take any decisions in a conglomerated fashion… Decisions were taking by Rahmqvist together maybe with Erwee, but I think I should believe it’s Leif in particular… V/O Rahmqvist even demanded Veto rights as a member of the Mapungubwe Foundation board… Eugene I think Mr. Rahmqvist wasn't going to let anybody share his idea, share his running of this place, So there were quite a lot of conflict from the early meetings… Makwela I remember in one previous meeting wherein Leif just banged the door and went out because we said we wanted to see financial statement. And then he said no, I'll also want to see financial statement of Dirisanang.”. Are you telling me that this man displayed such arrogance towards this community and the local municipality did nothing but watched. 00:17:56:06 - 00:18:35:06 Speaker 2 And know the local news to actually do to foot with your first question? Yes, he displays arrogance, but the municipality did almost everything in its power to make it a point that it brings them to the table… V/O By 2015 the relationship between The Drop-In Centre and Rahmqvist was crumbling. Rahmqvist appointed Sarkie Mateke as Orphanage mother… which meant that 2 different charities were operating from the same municipal property – Rahmqvist’s Orphanage inside the newly constructed building … and the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre, in a corrugated iron shack along the fence of the property. V/O Manager of the Blouberg Municipality satellite office in Alldays, Frans Mphateng stepped in during our interview with Makwela to help explain the situation…. Frans Mphateng Frans: The thing is, some of the things were like hearsay up until we realised but this thing is real. Because we went there and Manangena took us along throughout that building and we could see that really, they are not utilising that very big building… V/O Despite the issues, Rahmqvist has over the years, brought many international guests to visit “his orphanage”... Paulina Every year, we will have visitors from Sweden coming in to check if work is being done, and they donate money. As we speak, they were here on Friday. A lot of white people were here on Friday. On Saturday they left and went to the farm. V/O While we were filming in Alldays, Rahmqvist was treating his guests to his extravagant 80th Birthday celebrations… BIRTHDAY CLIP V/O The community alleges that, when guests visit, children are enticed to spend an hour or two at the orphanage, to sing and pose for pictures… all to impress would-be donors… Stephen This guy, he gets lot of millions using our kids, and at the end our kids get nothing… V/O Rahmqvist responded in writing via his lawyer, Hennie Erwee. He denies all allegations and says the Drop-In Centre children are welcome at his facility. Both Erwee and Rahmqvist emphatically deny benefiting financially from any donations received for the orphanage, all of which can be accounted for… and they offered this video from the birthday celebrations, presumably as proof that Rahmqvist is supporting the community… UPS VIDEO “Happy Birthday, Father, and I thank God for giving us a father like you. And we thank you for the home you give us.” V/O Behind the girl giving the birthday wishes is Orphanage Mother, Sarkie Mateke. She claims she’s currently taking care of 19 children in the so-called Orphanage… V/O According to Rahmqvist and Erwee, all allegations against them are part of a smear campaign by former employee Eugene Small… Rahmqvist says he is suing Small for R30 million, which Small owes him… But Eugene maintains it’s a matter of principle… Eugene The main thing is people go out there, they gloat about what they’re doing. They write articles in magazines about what they do and how great they are. And the children who are supposed to benefit from the beginning, from 2014 that they're supposed to benefit, eat on the ground. V/O Rahmqvist and Erwee add that no children are deliberately sourced to mislead donors, and all donations received have been spent on running the orphanage, and other initiatives via a different NPC, The Rahmqvist Foundation. They claim the community members of the Mapungubwe Foundation board were eager to gain control of funds and ignored their attempts to convene board meetings. Frans Mphateng Masa: What are you going to do to make sure that those children, this winter, are not inside that shack… Frans: Like MAkwela has just said, the matter is with the HAWKS, what was left now was for the council to take a decision on whether to tell him to move out in terms of the document. Masa: Isn’t it a no-brainer that he should move out? Frans: No, in a case… as you are dealing with a case you can’t just abruptly say no today you must go… Masa: It’s not abrupt. I’m saying this thing has been going on since 2015, 2014. That’s a long time ago, Sir. Frans: Those were not… they were issues that we were discussing, we were trying to resolve… Masa: Had it been nipped in the bud then, do you think we’d be sitting in this position where you now have to get a council meeting to get rid of this man… Farns: Unless you realise that something really fishy is happening.. Masa: It’s really fishy… we spent 2 days.. Frans: It’s really fishy because we can all agree. That’s why we are saying we took the matter to the HAWKS. V/O The Hawks have confirmed that they are investigating the case, but could not give us any further information… And while board members are fighting and sending letters, pointing fingers at each other, the children of the Dirisinang Drop-In Centre are grateful for the little that they have… And Paulina and Stephen continue to fight for them… Stephen My wish is to die, this problem being solved.. If I can die, this problem not being solved… I think I can be a ghost… PROMOS PROMO 1 11” A so-called “Orphanage”, equipped with facilities, built specifically to improve the lives of these children… UPSOUND : STEPHEN Everything is nice inside… right for the kids So why are they not using it? PROMO 2 21” A registered NPO feeding over 100 vulnerable children, a multimillion rand centre built for them and the municipality that provided the land UPSOUND STEPHEN We were excited, very excited.. Everyone in the community we were very happy… So why are these children unable to access the building that was intended for them? PROMO 3 21” With no running water and no electricity a group of volunteers are feeding over 100 kids in the Alldays Community… UPSOUND: PAULINA This, right next to a R6 million building, constructed to benefit these children!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Millions donated for an orphanage that doesn't exist!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Swedish national Lief Rahmqvist is one of the biggest private landowners in the Limpopo Province. In 1994 he bought up a bunch of farms on the Botswana border, North of Alldays, in the Blouberg Local Municipality. He consolidated them into what he called the Mapungubwe Private Nature Reserve (PTY) Ltd. The property borders the Mapungubwe National Park. In 2013 decided to "give back" to the community of Alldays. He founded the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre NPO. In essence, he took over the established Dirisang Drop-in centre that has been around for years... And he proceeded to get donations from far and wide
metadata.Summary: The Dirisang Drop-in Centre is a registered NPO with the Limpopo DSD, and for years, two volunteers, Stephen Serakalala and Paulina Manengene have been feeding kids from a little shack next to the Alldays Primary School. They also offer homework support to some of the most vulnerable children in Alldays... Come rain or shine, meals are cooked in the open and kids sit there on the dusty ground enjoying what is often their only meal for the day. In 2013 Rahmqvist swooped in as the saviour of these children. He founded the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre (NPO) and Stephen and Paulina were given positions on the board. (along with other municipal officers). And the building was built on Municipal land right next to the Alldays Primary School.
metadata.Further information: Today, Paulina and Stephen are still feeding 109 of the most vulnerable children in Alldays. Except, they do it in the dust NEXT TO the building built for them. They are not allowed to use the facility at all. They erected a tin shack from where they cook on gas (no electricity). They get water from a neighbour in a blue drum that they roll down the street once a week, as they are not allowed to access the water on the property. The children are also not allowed to use the ablution facilities (built for them)... so once again, Stephen managed to get 2x bucket toilets donated... and this is what the kids have to use. So, how is it possible that a haven was built for these kids in Alldays, but they have no access to it... in the meantime Rahmqvist boasts about his "Orphanage in South Africa" on social media. Even his lawyer, Hennie Erwee, names the "Orphanage" as his CSI project. Rahmqvist now lives abroad, but visits his farm regularly. When he has guests, he likes to take them to his Orphanage. The Orphanage Mother, Sarkie, then arranges children to come hang out at the building during the day for the publicity... in the evening, when the guests have left, they go home. These kids are not orphans. And the facility is not registered with DSD. What is registered is the Dirisang Drop-In Centre which operates in the corner of the property, while Sarkie pretty much lives alone in the building. When Rahmqvist set out to build the "Orphanage" he engaged with the municipality and got permission to use the land. He got a Swedish architect and local contractors to build his orphanage... All along, he maintained that he wanted to retain sole power, but this is not how NPO's work. The Mapungubwe Foundation NPO Board consists of Rahmqvist, his lawyer, Hennie Erwee, Stephen and Paulina from the Dirisang Drop-In Centre, 2 gentlemen from the Blouberg Local Municipality and 2 others. Mr Machaba -- who was the Blouberg Municipal Manager at the time -- was elected as Chairman of the Board... and he still is... In 2013 Rahmqvist started building his Orphanage. The original plan was to build an orphanage for 300 kids... But eventually a building was built with room for about 10 girls and 10 boys. At the same time, he decided to build a lodge (Lesedi Lodge) on one of his farms. He made a deal with all contractors working on the Orphanage that he would deduct a donation of 6.5% from their fee as a donation to the orphanage. Emails also show other donations from various international individuals and companies. In 2014 a container with donated goods, including 40 beds arrived from Sweden. Even though Rahmqvist sent a letter to the Department of Trade and Industry, declaring that the beds were a donation to be used in the Orphanage... and even though he advertised on social media about the generous donation of beds... The beds were taken to Lesedi Lodge. In 2008 Micawber 639 (PTY) Ltd applied for prospecting rights on Rahmqvist's property, which was granted. One of the directors of Micawber 639 is Hendrik Marthinus Erwee (Hennie Erwee) who also happens to be Rahmqvist's lawyer. In 2013 when Rahmqvist started with the "orphanage", a young Indian mining company wanted to prospect for coal on Rahmqvist's land. IG Resources FZE negotiated with Rahmqvist and Erwee and they were given permission to prospect under the mining licence of Micawber 639. They also generously committed to paying a R2.9 million donation to Rahmqvist's "Orphanage"... Websites, and press releases and newspaper articles painted Rahmqvist a saint, a saviour. Rahmqvist also insisted that all his staff and even the hunters hired to facilitate hunts on his farms, pay a 6.5% donation to the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre / Orphanage. Rahmqvist boasts online about his CSI project, helping desperate children. The international company (which was started by Erik Rahmqvist) lists the "Orphanage" as their main CSI project. Mr Erwee (attorney and Mining Director) also owns a company called The Ark Wildlife Exporters, facilitating hunts, and the export of hunting trophies... And yes... he also brags about the Alldays Orphanage on his company/s websites. Everyone, it seems, is using these hungry, desperate children to score brownie points with the outside world! But the not-so-funny thing is... It's been a decade and those kids are still fed from a little shack on the side of the property. In 40degrees they sit in the sun, Meters away from the building, doing their homework, eating the meal that Paulina and Stephen prepared in a make-shift kitchen. Rahmqvist was not transparent about the donations received and fights broke out between him and the other board members. And even though the other Board Members instituted a Vote of No Confidence in Rahmqvist and Erwee, the 2 are still in charge. The Hawks have been investigating. Nature conservation is investigating various transgressions, from illegal logging on his farm, to illegal logging inside Botswana, to illegal Hunts on his farm... And while everyone drag their feet, the building stands almost empty and Rahmqvist and Erwee have time to cover their tracks. The 25000HA farm is listed as for sale -- for US$58 million Rahmqvist has instigated litigation against those who speak out. Erwee is good friends with Dawie Groenewald -- SA Rhino Poacher No.1 & John Hume, Mr Rhino Breeder... Erwee's company - The Ark Wildlife Exporters has an office in China. Rahmqvist's farm borders the Mapungubwe National Park and Mapungubwe has rhinos and few fences... In the meantime Rahmqvist has handed over the management of the "Orphanage" to NorSA, an NGO run by Erwee's ex-wife, Marietjie Bezuidenhout... Without the consent of the other board members.
